task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Independently re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself, not from CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary (which you should treat as a claim to verify, not a fact to copy) -- see core-directives.md's 'Every producing step has a validating step'. Check specifically:
1. Does the design cover every one of ISS-0451's three acceptance criteria (docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml): AC1 (a persistent-fault test scenario proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive), AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic showing the fix tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle), AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests)?
2. Is the arithmetic in the design actually correct? Work it through yourself rather than trusting the doc's own numbers -- re-derive independently whether the chosen top-level restart-intensity value plus the circuit-breaker's trip threshold genuinely prevents an indefinite persistent fault from ever exhausting the top-level supervisor's budget (not merely delaying it by a bounded, finite number of extra cycles).
3. Does the design contain any implementation code (.ex function bodies)? If it names a new module (e.g. a PollersBreaker GenServer), it should specify signatures/@specs/state-shape/callback contracts only -- fail this check if you find an actual function body implementing logic, not just a signature.
4. Is the design unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without having to invent any missing decision (exact config keys, exact state machine transitions, exact backoff schedule values, exact module/file placement)?
5. Does the design explicitly state how REQ-219's own AC2 (boot order: Infrastructure before Pollers) and AC4 (single Pollers-budget-exhaustion event still leaves Infrastructure/Http alone) are preserved, with reasoning you can independently verify against the current code (lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex)?
6. Is the specified regression-test mechanism (how the test keeps the fault persistent, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test which clears it) concrete enough for TEST-DESIGNER to build without design ambiguity?

This is a hard gate -- FAIL with specific, itemized gaps (per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail worked example) if any check above doesn't pass; do not rubber-stamp.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict states explicitly, per ISS-0451 AC, whether AC1/AC2/AC3 are each covered by the design
Verdict states the validator's own independently re-derived arithmetic check result, not a repetition of CODE-DESIGNER's numbers
Verdict states explicitly whether any implementation code was found in the design doc
Verdict states explicitly whether REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning is checked and correct
A FAIL verdict lists every gap by section/line with what must change; a PASS verdict states what was independently re-derived and how
task.regate_note: RE-GATE (iteration 2): CODE-DESIGNER fixed the iteration-1 defect you found -- section 3.4a's children-list snippet now reads `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used directly as the children-list entry (not the broken {module, arg} 2-tuple form). Per handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-02-code-designer.json's own result.summary, CODE-DESIGNER also independently re-verified this live (10 repeated kill/restart cycles against a max_restarts: 1 top-level supervisor, confirmed it stayed alive throughout), and separately found and fixed a SECOND defect while re-deriving: Supervisor.restart_child/2 cannot restart an already-exited :temporary child (OTP deletes its child spec on termination -- returns {:error, :not_found}), which broke every PollersBreaker restart call the design specified AND the EXISTING test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's own restart_pollers!/0 helper (terminate_child then restart_child) used in the AC4 test body and its teardown. Both were corrected to Supervisor.start_child/2 with the full child spec. Re-check with full rigor, not a lighter second-look pass: (1) verify the corrected 3.4a snippet actually applies :temporary (re-derive yourself, don't trust the producer's claim of having verified it); (2) verify the start_child/2-vs-restart_child/2 fix is correct and complete -- check every call site in the design doc that restarts Pollers, and confirm the claim about the EXISTING pollers_test.exs test needing this same fix is accurate against that file's actual current content; (3) re-check section 4's arithmetic; (4) re-check REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation reasoning under both fixes; (5) re-check section 6's test spec for internal consistency now that restart_pollers!/0 itself needs changing; (6) confirm no implementation code. This is iteration 2 of 3 -- one rework attempt remains after this if it fails again.

result.summary:
RE-GATE iteration 2: PASS, independently re-derived, not copied from CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary. AC1/AC2/AC3 (ISS-0451): all three covered. AC1 (persistent-fault regression test proving Letflow.Supervisor/Repo/Bandit survive) -- section 6 specifies a concrete new test file (test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs), reuses the existing force_poller_crash seam WITHOUT clearing it, and names exact observables (Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor) unchanged, a Process.monitor/:DOWN check on the top-level pid, Repo/Infrastructure/Http pids unchanged) asserted WHILE the fault is still active -- covered. AC2 (documented restart-intensity arithmetic tolerating at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle) -- section 4's arithmetic re-derived independently: because Pollers' child spec is genuinely restart: :temporary (confirmed live, see below), Pollers-attributable restarts consume exactly 0 of the top level's own max_restarts budget for any fault duration, so 0 <= max_restarts holds unconditionally -- this is stronger than 'tolerates one cycle,' it tolerates indefinite persistence by construction -- covered. AC3 (no regression to REQ-219's own AC2 boot-order or AC4 single-crash-isolation tests) -- AC2 is untouched (verified: :restart is a child-spec key that only governs post-exit behavior, never start sequencing, and the children list order Infrastructure-then-Pollers-then-Http is preserved with PollersBreaker inserted after Pollers). AC4's OBSERVABLE property (single crash still isolates Infrastructure/Http) is preserved, but its MECHANISM changes and the design correctly identifies and specifies the resulting required edits to the EXISTING test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs (verified against that file's actual current content, not the design's paraphrase -- see below) -- covered, with the required existing-test changes explicitly flagged as in-scope, not deferred.

Independent re-derivation performed (all live, Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29, this project's pinned toolchain, matching the design's own citations):
1. Section 3.4a corrected snippet: ran `Supervisor.child_spec({Worker, restart: :temporary}, [])` (the OLD, broken 2-tuple form) vs `Supervisor.child_spec(Worker, restart: :temporary)` (the corrected form used as the children-list entry). Confirmed live: the 2-tuple form produces NO :restart key (threads the keyword list into start_link's arg instead, defaults :permanent); the corrected form produces a genuine %{restart: :temporary, ...} spec. The design's citation is accurate, not merely trusted.
2. start_child/2 vs restart_child/2: built a live top-level supervisor (max_restarts: 1) with one :temporary child. Confirmed: after killing the child once, Process.whereis returns nil (no auto-restart, top level stays alive); Supervisor.restart_child/2 against the already-exited :temporary child returns {:error, :not_found} exactly as claimed (OTP deletes a :temporary child's spec on exit); Supervisor.start_child/2 with the full child_spec correctly restarts it, returns {:error, {:already_started, pid}} as a safe no-op when called on a live child; Supervisor.terminate_child/2 on a :temporary child ALSO deletes its spec immediately (which_children -> [], subsequent restart_child/2 -> {:error, :not_found}) -- confirming the design's 'SECOND CORRECTION' claim about the EXISTING pollers_test.exs's restart_pollers!/0 helper (lines 217-221: terminate_child then `{:ok, _pid} = restart_child(...)`) genuinely breaking with a MatchError once Pollers is :temporary, verified against that file's actual current content (read fresh, lines 116-119 inline call site and 217-221 helper definition and its two call sites at line 99 on_exit and inline at 118 both confirmed to match the design's citations exactly). Ran 10 repeated kill/start_child cycles against the max_restarts:1 top-level supervisor -- it survived all 10, confirming start_child/2-issued restarts never touch the top level's own intensity counter (the load-bearing fact section 4's arithmetic depends on). Also independently confirmed which_children/1 against an unregistered supervisor name exits :noproc rather than returning [] -- validating section 6.2 step 6's correction that Process.whereis(...) == nil, not which_children, is the only valid 'Pollers is genuinely stopped' observable.
3. Section 4 arithmetic re-checked: the '5 - 0 = 5' framing is logically sound given the now-proven 0-consumption invariant; margin for the 3 remaining :permanent top-level children (Infrastructure/Http/PollersBreaker) is strictly >= the pre-design margin of 3 for the same three-child class. Confirmed application.ex currently has no max_restarts/max_seconds override (OTP default 3/5 genuinely governs today, matching the design's stated premise).
4. REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation re-checked against current lib/letflow/application.ex and lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex: AC2 unaffected (children list order preserved, :restart does not influence start sequencing -- basic, verifiable OTP semantics). AC4's observable preserved; mechanism-change consequences for the EXISTING test correctly and completely identified (both the assertion at lines 152-161 depending on an automatic top-level restart, and the restart_pollers!/0 helper at lines 217-221 used at both its call sites).
5. Section 6 regression-test spec re-checked for internal consistency: step 3 explicitly avoids the old restart_pollers!/0 pattern and uses terminate_child + start_child/2 directly instead -- no circular dependency on the now-broken helper.
6. No implementation code found: grepped the full document for def/defp/handle_info bodies -- the only function body present (`def init(arg), do: {:ok, arg}`) is inside the throwaway ProbeCD.Worker demonstration module used to cite live OTP behavior, not part of the PollersBreaker design itself, consistent with this project's design-vs-implementation convention and the same class of evidence already accepted in iteration 1's gate. PollersBreaker's own state machine (3.2, 3.4, 3.6) is specified as prose, a state-transition table, and call-site descriptions (which OTP function is invoked, with what arguments) -- never as an actual .ex function body implementing control flow.

All five prior BLOCKERs (iterations 0 and 1) are resolved and did not recur. Design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without inventing a missing decision: exact module name/file path, exact children-list snippet, exact state shape (@type t()), exact backoff table (5 concrete values with rationale), exact config value (max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 5), and exact required edits to the existing test file are all named. Q1-Q3 (open questions) are correctly scoped as non-AC-blocking judgment calls, not missing decisions the design was required to make.
result.next_action: Proceed to TEST-DESIGNER per WF-03 -- design gate passed, rework iteration 2 of 3 succeeded.

gate_history.summary: Design's §4 margin arithmetic ('5 - 2 = 3') assumed PollersBreaker's terminate_child call always beat the top-level Supervisor's own automatic restart-on-exit for the same child crash. Independently re-derived and found unproven: no OTP guarantee that the breaker's monitor-message-then-synchronous-call chain completes before the top-level Supervisor's direct in-process EXIT reaction.
issues: BLOCKER: unproven race in the breaker's termination-vs-automatic-restart ordering, undermining AC2's arithmetic (full text in this run's git history, commit 4e127a7d).
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- either restart: :temporary on Pollers' child spec (removes race structurally) or cite an actual OTP ordering guarantee and re-derive the margin.

gate_history.summary: Rework iteration 1's fix (restart: :temporary via a {Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary} children-list entry) correctly diagnoses that :temporary would remove the race by construction, and correctly describes :temporary's OTP semantics (independently confirmed against lib/elixir/lib/supervisor.ex and a live probe on this project's pinned Elixir 1.20.3). But the specific children-list syntax used does not actually apply the :temporary override -- a 2-tuple {module, arg} children-list entry threads `arg` into the child's start_link call, not into Supervisor.child_spec/2's override keys, so the resulting child spec still defaults to :permanent. The original race from iteration 0 is therefore still live under this design as written.
issues: BLOCKER: §3.4a's `{Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary}` children-list syntax does not set restart: :temporary -- verified live that this exact form yields a child spec with no :restart override (Supervisor.child_spec/2's overrides parameter is never invoked by this syntax); the corrected form is `Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)` used as the children-list entry, confirmed live to work correctly.
BLOCKER: §3.6/§4's arithmetic and 'exactly 0 top-level restarts, structurally' claim depend on the broken syntax and are unproven as a result -- must be re-derived against the corrected snippet.

BLOCKER: §5's claim that the existing pollers_test.exs AC4 test 'will fail as written' is false under the design's actual (broken) syntax -- that test would keep passing, since the top level still auto-restarts Pollers today; must be restated once §3.4a is fixed.
BLOCKER: §6.2 step 6's `Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil` observable is not reliably true under the broken syntax for the same reason.
gate_history.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER -- fix §3.4a's children-list syntax to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) (or equivalent explicit map form), then re-derive §3.6/§3.7/§4's arithmetic and restate §5/§6.2 step 6 against the corrected mechanism. Rework iteration 2 of 3.

gate_history.summary: Iteration 2 corrects §3.4a's children-list syntax to Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary) and fixes the newly-discovered restart_child/2-vs-start_child/2 defect across every restart call site (PollersBreaker's :closed-branch and :half_open_probe handlers, plus the EXISTING pollers_test.exs's restart_pollers!/0 helper). Independently re-derived with full rigor, not a lighter pass: re-ran the corrected Supervisor.child_spec/2 probe live and confirmed it genuinely applies :temporary (the broken 2-tuple form does not); built a live top-level supervisor (max_restarts: 1) with a :temporary child and confirmed restart_child/2 on an already-exited :temporary child returns {:error, :not_found}, start_child/2 with the full spec correctly restarts it, terminate_child/2 on a :temporary child also deletes its spec, and 10 kill/start_child cycles never touched the top level's max_restarts:1 budget. Verified the design's citations of pollers_test.exs's actual current content (lines 99, 116-119, 152-161, 217-221) against the file itself, not the design's paraphrase -- all accurate. Re-checked §4's arithmetic (0-consumption invariant holds given the live-confirmed :temporary behavior), REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation (AC2 unaffected since :restart never governs start order; AC4's observable preserved, mechanism-change consequences for the existing test correctly and completely identified), and §6's regression-test spec for internal consistency now that restart_pollers!/0 itself needs replacing. No implementation code found -- the sole function body present is inside a throwaway probe module demonstrating OTP's own child_spec/2 semantics, not part of the PollersBreaker design.
